Juicing is actually a great way to get a natural nutritional boost. The problem is, too many people use it to make fruit juices rather than more exotic, nutritional, drinks. Juicing used to be about using ingredients like kale, lettuce, celery, spinach, carrots, and other oddball (radish) vegetables. In which something like apples and carrots would be added to make it palatable - just barely. One of the more famous concoctions of old is "green drink." Which is now a genetic term for just about any juiced drink which is green. Properly prepared, it's extremely nutrient dense, coming in at less than 100 calories. Before someone says, "take supplements", many supplements are not well absorbed but is dramatically improved when delivered via drink. There are other nutrients which are not normally part of supplements. This is especially true for things like iron, which may have have low absorption rates, or require other nutrients to be properly absorbed and used. Which is why it's supposed to be a low dose, daily intake (example, cooking on ironware). Nature tends to provide them in proper ratios.

Alright, side note here -

People have given somewhat of a backlash to juicing, and for good reason - fruit juice is basically just sugar water without the fiber and some of the nutrients from the fruit.

However, I have a juicer that I make use of regularly, to good effect. Vegetables. At the end of the week, before I go grocery shopping, I gather up the greens and veggies I didn't use during the prior week, before they get old. Some of them I dehydrate, but I usually have some to throw through a masticating juicer. This puts out a dry-ish pulp that's good for composting, and the liquid from the veggies. It's not very tasty on its own, and sometimes I use it for cooking something tastier. But I usually just drink it. It's not as tasty as fruit juice because it's not full of sugar, but it's still packed with a significant amount of the nutrients that were in the veggies. It doesn't have any fiber, but since I'm not downing a bunch of sugar I don't need fiber to slow the blood sugar spike. Even with the loss of fiber and some nutrients, it's a lot better than losing all the nutrients from veggies that I probably would have let go bad soon.

I highly recommend a decent masticating juicer and making veggie juice.
